title: Work done: when does a force really do work?
examples: What is work done in physics?
How do you calculate work done?

explain.say: Here is a surprise. You can push a wall until you are sweaty and tired, and a scientist will say you did no work at all! In physics, work has a special meaning. Let us find out what it is.

draw.text: Work done: when does a force really do work?

explain.say: Look at the bag being dragged. Your pull is 50 newtons, and the bag moves 4 metres. Work done is force times distance moved: 50 times 4 makes 200 joules. A joule is the unit of energy. How far did the bag move?

4 metres, yes! Now look: you push a wall with all your might, but it does not move at all. Distance is zero, so the work done is zero. You still get tired, because your muscles use energy inside you. Does the arrow move anything here?

No, nothing moves! Now lift a bag up onto a shelf. Your lift is 100 newtons, its weight, and you raise it 1.5 metres. That is 100 times 1.5, which makes 150 joules of work, now stored as gravitational energy. Which way does the bag move?

forces.label: Your lift 100 N
forces.ask: How much work does lifting take?

explain.say: Up, against gravity, well done! So work means energy transferred by a force moving something. Wow fact: climbing a 3 metre flight of stairs, a 50 kilogram person does about 1500 joules of work. Challenge: how much work is it to drag a sledge with 20 newtons for 10 metres?

forces.label: Your lift 100 N
forces.ask: How much work does lifting take?

faq.a: Work done is the energy transferred when a force moves an object. Work equals force times the distance moved in the direction of the force.
Not in physics. The wall does not move, so the distance is zero and no work is done on it, even though your muscles get tired.
asks: Why is no work done pushing a wall?

faq.q: How much work does lifting take?
faq.a: Lifting work equals the object's weight times the height raised. Lifting 100 newtons by 1.5 metres takes 150 joules.
A joule is the unit of work and energy. One joule is the work done when a 1 newton force moves something 1 metre.

faq.q: Where does the energy go when you do work?
faq.a: It moves into another store, like gravitational energy when lifting, or heat from friction when dragging something along the floor.

facts: Work done (J) = force (N) × distance moved in the direction of the force (m).
1 joule is the work done by a 1 newton force moving through 1 metre.

quiz.say: You push a box with 40 N for 5 m. How much work do you do?
quiz.show: You push a box with 40 N for 5 m. How much work do you do?

quiz.show: In which case is NO work done on the object?
quiz.why: If the object does not move, the distance is zero, so no work is done on it.
